long_biography.plain_text:
Kambourides grew up in Cyprus, attended public schools and reached international mathematics competitions before studying mechanical engineering and mathematics at MIT on scholarships. He entered real-estate private equity at Goldman Sachs and later became a founding partner of Soros Real Estate Partners. There he worked on property outsourcing and investment strategy across Europe and Japan.

In 2004 he launched Dolphin Capital Partners, pairing investment management with hands-on development of hospitality and residential destinations. The firm became known for projects created with international hotel brands, while Kambourides widened his entrepreneurial work into immersive museums, design, finance and digital ventures. He established MIT's first doctoral fellowship in computational engineering in 2008, funding tuition, fees and stipends for graduate researchers.
